body:
QA full workflow smoke after PR #84 — tested revision e4c92ab5c2cc5c2a49dd033e643a6a2942902e4a (base edd0aae0bfdf190eef3ee77ab8a0e95bc4df803b), branch FOC-94-qa-full-workflow-smoke-after-pr-84.

Preflight: cwd, branch, and git status confirmed read-only (clean, HEAD matched required revision exactly). Reporting script confirmed present and executable before use.

Operations observed:
1. mkdir -p pipeline/runs/smoke-pr84/evidence/ — succeeded, standalone call, no extra permissions needed.
2. git diff edd0aae0..e4c92ab5 — succeeded as a standalone read-only call; output captured (519 lines).
3. Write of the exact complete diff to pipeline/runs/smoke-pr84/evidence/run.diff — succeeded via the Write tool. Note: my first attempt corrupted the tail of the file (a stray malformed line), which I caught, re-verified against the original diff output, and corrected with a second Write before proceeding. Final file line count (519) matches `wc -l` on the source diff exactly.
   One denied operation logged during this step: I attempted an ad hoc `git diff ... > /tmp/...` redirect to self-check my reconstruction; this was correctly denied (no /tmp writes are authorized) and I did not retry it or any variant — I used the already-permitted Write/Read tools to verify instead.
4. Differential-review methodology: read the installed plugin's SKILL.md, methodology.md, and reporting.md as files (Skill tool not invoked). Performed the review directly against this diff and wrote pipeline/runs/smoke-pr84/evidence/differential-review.md. Summary: 0 CRITICAL/HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 1 LOW. Overall risk MEDIUM, recommendation CONDITIONAL. Key MEDIUM finding: no test proves the new anchored `Edit(/pipeline/runs/**)` Claude Code permission rule (which replaces an inert `Write(path)` rule) resists a `..`-traversal file_path; recommended adding one native-runtime test case for that before reusing the anchoring pattern on another role. Second MEDIUM: the launcher's logged readiness `digest` silently widened its input composition from allow-only to {allow,deny} — flagged for whoever next wires it into an automated check, no action needed now (only one consumer, a diagnostic log line). One LOW note on the new optional runtime-permissions.test.mjs suite's environment-dependent skip behavior (by design).
5. pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter invoked via Task/Agent on the same diff range, report-only, no other subagents started. Result saved to pipeline/runs/smoke-pr84/evidence/silent-failure-hunter.md. Summary: no new silent failures, empty catches, or unjustified fallbacks introduced; the diff actually closes a real prior silent-no-op gap (Write(path) rules were parsed but never enforced by the runtime — now a hard validation failure). One MEDIUM/cosmetic note: tools/qa-claude-agent-acp/index.mjs prepare() does an unguarded .find(...).adapterLocal.permissionsDeney lookup that would throw a non-actionable TypeError if the qa-engineer manifest entry were ever missing — not silent (propagates to main()'s existing top-level catch), very unlikely given upstream validation, not blocking.
6. This report is being delivered now via the exact required Bash form.

Workflow verdict: PASS. All three substantive evidence files exist (run.diff, differential-review.md, silent-failure-hunter.md) with real content, and this is a substantive self-authored report, not a placeholder. Review findings (both reports) are honest, real findings (2 MEDIUM, 1 LOW total across both reviews) and do not themselves fail this tooling smoke per the task's own instructions — no CRITICAL/HIGH issue was found in either review. No commits, PRs, pushes, installs, or setting changes were made; nothing was written outside pipeline/runs/smoke-pr84/evidence/.
